title: Synergistic strength–plasticity enhancement via multi-type nanoprecipitates and ultrafine retained austenite in Cu/Ni/Al/V-alloyed medium-Mn steels
abstract: To overcome the strength-plasticity trade-off and single-precipitate strengthening ceiling in medium-Mn steels (MMS), this study developed a novel quenching-partitioning-tempering-aging (Q&PT-A) process for Cu/Ni/Al/V-alloyed MMS, realizing synergistic regulation of multi-type nanoprecipitates (VC, Cu-rich, NiAl) and ultrafine retained austenite (RA). Systematic investigation revealed a competition between austenite stabilization/reversion and multi-type precipitation, modulated by quenching temperature. Quenching to 180 °C generated the desired fresh martensite, providing nucleation sites and driving force for Cu–NiAl co-precipitation while promoting austenite reversion during the subsequent aging. Such an unreported microstructural design finally results in excellent tensile properties (1965 ± 22 MPa ultimate tensile strength, 1625 ± 19 MPa yield strength, 8.4 ± 0.6% total elongation), attributed to the coupled effects of multi-type precipitation strengthening and ultrafine RA-induced transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP). We conclude that the pre-aging microstructure dominates the performance of multi-precipitate-hardened MMS, and the Q&PT-A process enables tailored mechanical properties for diverse applications, offering a novel theoretical and technical pathway for high-strength, balanced-performance MMS.
